title: timeboxed-playbook-staging-matrix-and-synthetic-probe-harness
author: Ethan Cole
release_notes: Adds a timeboxed playbook staging matrix runner with synthetic probe harness and configurable safety gates. Enables opt-in rehearsal runs from Console and CLI. Includes e2e tests and docs for operators.
description:
Motivation: On-call teams need a lightweight, low-risk way to validate playbook changes across a spectrum of temporal constraints (fast recovery vs slow remediation) and environmental conditions. This PR introduces a staging matrix runner that exercises a playbook against a configurable set of temporal windows and synthetic probes to surface regressions in timing, ordering, and side-effect detection before a playbook reaches production.

What this does (single string): Adds a new 'staging matrix' mode to the playbook rehearsal framework that: 1) accepts a matrix definition (timeboxes, probe profiles, injected-failure rates), 2) runs playbook steps deterministically in a sandboxed runner with injectable probe responses, 3) evaluates safety gates (side-effect detection, external API call thresholds, tenant-impact heuristics), and 4) emits compact rollup reports and actionable remediation hints. Includes a CLI entrypoint (slo-stg) and a Console toggle to schedule matrix runs against a branch or a playbook version.

Checklist:
- [x] core runner implementation (worker + scheduler)
- [x] synthetic probe harness and five probe templates (http-latency, db-timeout, partial-ack, metric-dip, permission-deny)
- [x] safety gate framework with abort/retry policies
- [x] opt-in Console UI hook and CLI flag --staging-matrix
- [x] end-to-end tests with deterministic seeds
- [x] docs and migration notes

Compatibility: The staging runner uses the existing playbook step interface and sandbox adapter; no changes required to user playbooks. A new opt-in annotation stanza is available for playbooks that want to declare external side-effects to improve safety gate accuracy.

Risk and mitigation: The harness executes steps in an isolated sandbox; by default the runner runs in 'dry-run' mode that will not perform external writes. The safety gates add a conservative abort if any configured side-effect threshold is reached. Default scheduler concurrency is low (2 parallel matrices) to limit resource churn.

Migration notes: Operators can opt-in per-namespace. See migration_notes field for CLI bootstrap steps.

Rollout: start with internal teams (infra, platform) for 2 weeks, expand to early adopter customers behind feature flag, monitor the 'rehearsal-failures' metric and abort-rate.

Related work: builds on ENG-4921 (playbook validator) and complements the quieter synthetic-probe work in ENG-4988.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial runner scaffold; probe harness and templates; safety-gate DSL; CLI and Console hook; e2e seeded tests; docs and examples; CI flakiness fixes.
review_conversation:
Priya: 'Nice ergonomics. Two questions: can the probe templates be extended at runtime and what's the expected resource per-matrix?'
Author (Ethan): 'Probe templates are data-driven and load from /etc/slo/probes or S3; we'll add a runtime catalog in a follow-up (ENG-5012). Default resource per-matrix is configured as a cgroup of 500m CPU and 256Mi RAM; can be tuned per-namespace.'
Marco: 'Please add explicit unit tests for the safety_gate abort path and for permission-deny probe.'
Author: 'Added targeted tests and increased coverage on safety_gates; see commit 4/7.'
Susan: 'Approve with one nit: CLI flag name should be --staging-matrix not --staging. Also add a short note in migration docs that dry-run is default.'
Author: 'Addressed both nits; updated docs. Marking as ready.'
CI: initial e2e job failed due to a race in seeded tests; fixed by introducing deterministic seeding and retry logic. Final CI run: all checks passed.
Merge: squashed after approvals and merged to main on 2026-02-03.
migration_notes: How to opt-in: 1) Install new slo-toolkit release (>= v2.14.0). 2) Run `slo-stg bootstrap --namespace infra` to create sandbox RBAC and probe catalog. 3) Annotate playbooks that perform external writes with 'side_effects: true' to enable stricter safety gates. 4) Start with --staging-matrix --dry-run to review rollup reports before enabling write mode.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal infra + platform teams for 2 weeks behind feature flag. Phase 2: open to early-adopter customers with a 1-day cadence and max 3 concurrent matrices. Phase 3: GA with Console toggle and default dry-run preserving backward compatibility. Monitor metrics: rehearsal.aborts, rehearsal.duration.p95, rehearsal.side_effect_alerts.
notes_on_testing: Added deterministic e2e tests with mocked probe responses and a seeded random generator. Local dev: use `pytest tests/e2e/test_staging_matrix_seeded.py -k quick` or `slo-stg run --example readonly-playbook.yaml --seed 42` to reproduce runs. CI includes a separate workflow that runs the full matrix once per day to detect flakiness.
safety_assurance: Dry-run default, sandbox adapter, conservative abort thresholds, RBAC-restricted probe catalog updates. Ops must explicitly enable write-mode per-namespace.
